minutes.headline: ZBA granted both special permits: a 15-foot setback relief for a three-bay garage and reconstruction of a duplex at Laurel Lane.
minutes.summary: The board held two hearings. The first, for a three-bay attached garage on Barrett/Bird Street, drew no public comment and was granted. The second, to rebuild a non-conforming house at 68 Laurel Lane as a duplex, drew neighbor concerns about rentals, driveway traffic and a possible second duplex; it was granted after the owner said she would live in one unit.

public_comment.topic: Surprised the application lacked house plans and was a duplex; worried about a loophole and about four families on a small lot.
Concerned the duplexes would become rental properties changing the character of a long-time single-family neighborhood; asked about rental versus owner-occupied rules.
A resident asked whether setback requirements are the same for single-family and duplex, and later asked about bedroom layout and unit size of the new building.

votes.motion: Grant special permit dimensional variation for 15 feet of relief for the three-bay garage as per submitted plan
votes.outcome: passed (several ayes heard; count not stated)

votes.motion: Approve special permit to reconstruct a structure on the same footprint of a pre-existing non-conforming lot at 68 Laurel Lane

decisions.decision: Special permit for the attached garage declared granted with standard conditions and appeal instructions.
Special permit for 68 Laurel Lane declared granted with standard conditions and appeal instructions.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals granted a special permit for 68 Laurel Lane, allowing a non-conforming house to be rebuilt as a duplex on the same footprint.
The board granted a special permit for dimensional relief of 15 feet for a three-bay attached garage; ayes were heard and the count was not stated.
Neighbors at the Laurel Lane hearing raised concerns about rentals, driveway traffic and a possible second duplex on the lot.
The Laurel Lane permit was declared granted with standard conditions and appeal instructions, after the owner said she would live in one unit.

why_it_matters: Special permits like these change what can be built on a lot, so they shape neighborhood density and traffic, but they carry no town budget line.
Neighbors who object to a granted permit have a limited window to appeal, which the board's decision instructions describe.
